sections.h2: Where to go for tax questions
sections.html:
The county Tax Department at 230 Government Center Drive, Wilmington, values real estate, mails the bills and takes payments. Call (910) 798-7300. The reappraisal team also answers email at reappraisal@nhcgov.com.

A bill is built from two pieces: your assessed value and a rate per $100 adopted by the county and municipal boards, normally in June. Assessed value is 100% of estimated market value as of the latest revaluation.

The county's general rate for fiscal year 2026-2027 is 30.6 cents per $100. Wilmington and three beach towns add rates of their own on top of that.

Rates in cents per $100, fiscal year 2026-2027

New Hanover County30.6

Houses outside town limits also pay a stormwater services fee, shown as a separate line on the bill.

Bills are due September 1. You can pay with no interest through January 5, and after that the interest rules in G.S. 105-360 apply.

Each bill has four coupons, one per quarter of the total, so you can pay in installments. Ways to pay:

  • Debit or credit card, or an e-check, at the Tax Office counter.
  • InvoiceCloud online, which adds a service fee, or by phone at 1-877-309-0878.
  • The drop box outside, just right of the Government Center entrance.
  • A check mailed to PO Box 18000, Wilmington, NC 28406.

If your lender pays from escrow you will get a courtesy notice. Confirm the lender really paid. Should January 5 be at risk of slipping by, call the office before January 6 and ask about a payment plan.

New Hanover reappraises every four years, although state law only requires eight. The commissioners picked four in 2008 because the county was growing fast, and the first four-year round took effect January 1, 2012. Current values are as of January 1, 2025, and the next revaluation is set for January 1, 2029.

Appraisers sort roughly 115,000 parcels into about 1,500 neighborhoods, study home and land sales, review parcels in the field and at a desk, and use aerial imagery and computer models. The result is a Schedule of Values that the commissioners must approve. Between revaluations, a parcel's value changes only for things like new building, damage, corrected records or a new use. Ordinary market swings wait for the next round.

A house still under construction on January 1 is taxed at whatever stage it has reached, then at full value the next year. You do not re-list real property each year, but new improvements must be reported in January, and Tax Department staff will do the listing if you ask.

sections.h2: What the value on your notice means
sections.html:
Assessed value is fair market value: the likeliest price an informed buyer and seller would agree on with neither rushed. What you paid, your insurance value and rebuilding cost are not the measure.

In a revaluation year the local boards publish a revenue-neutral rate, one that would raise the same money as the year before, and may adopt something higher or lower. A jump in value therefore does not guarantee a bigger bill, because the rate can move too. Look at both numbers before deciding to appeal.

The county's appeal form is free and you do not need a lawyer. Appeals open the day the value notice arrives and close when the review board adjourns each spring. Filing within 30 days of the notice is encouraged, because it gives staff time to review the file before any hearing.

The burden of proof is on you. Bring:

  • Sales of comparable homes that closed before January 1, 2025.
  • Photos showing condition or defects.
  • Notes on improvements the record gets wrong.
  • Optionally, a formal appraisal dated before January 1, 2025.

A dispute that survives informal review goes to the Board of Equalization and Review. Its members are local residents from brokerage, appraisal, construction and law, sitting in smaller panels. You may appear or send papers instead. The board meets from April to early May and issues a written ruling within 30 days. A further appeal goes to the state Property Tax Commission.

Any joint owner can file for the group. A business owner may send an officer, manager, W-2 employee or 25% owner. Other non-attorney helpers are limited to hardship cases such as illness, a death in the family or military deployment. Commercial owners are asked for three years of income and expense statements and a rent roll dated before January 1, 2025.

sections.h2: Exclusions for seniors, disabled owners and disabled veterans
sections.html:
Three state programs exist for older, disabled and disabled military owners. You can claim only one, and the application is Form AV-9, filed with the assessor.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: removes $25,000 or 50% of appraised value from taxation, whichever is larger, if 2026 income is within $38,800.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: removes the first $45,000 of value, with no age or income test.
  • Circuit breaker: caps the bill at 4.0% of income, or 5.0% for income above the ceiling and up to $58,200, for owners with five years in the home.

File in January if you can, though forms are accepted through June 1 before the tax year. Circuit breaker enrollees reapply yearly. Taxes above the cap are deferred, not waived, so a sale brings back the preceding three years.

A tax lien under G.S. 105-355 stays on the house through a sale. Call (910) 798-7300 for the balance and give the figure to the attorney or title agent running your closing.

If nothing is paid, the county can foreclose through the courts under G.S. 105-374. Paying the balance from sale proceeds closes off that path.

The usual sequence is simple. Get the payoff in writing, have it listed on the closing statement, and confirm afterward that the Tax Department posted the payment. A cash buyer can close quickly and skip lender steps, but the lien must still be cleared at the table.

sections.h2: Housing and prices in New Hanover County
sections.html: New Hanover County had 245,959 residents in 2025, up 9.0% from April 2020. A median owner-occupied house was worth $387,800 in the 2020 to 2024 data, with monthly owner costs of $1,888 with a mortgage and $658 without. Builders obtained 2,332 permits in 2025, so many owners have new work to report to the assessor.

faqs.q: Which day do New Hanover County property tax bills come due?
faqs.a: September 1. The county takes payment without interest until January 5, and interest starts January 6.

faqs.q: What is the county rate this fiscal year?
faqs.a: The county levies 30.6 cents per $100 for fiscal year 2026-2027, and unincorporated owners add 7.25 cents for fire services. Wilmington and the beach towns add municipal rates.
January 1, 2029. Values now in effect date from January 1, 2025.

faqs.q: Does it cost money to appeal a value?
faqs.a: No fee, and no attorney is needed. Sales and appraisals offered as evidence should predate January 1, 2025.

faqs.q: Who gets paid for taxes still owed at a sale?
faqs.a: The lien stays on the parcel until paid. Request the payoff figure from the Tax Department so the closing attorney can pay it from proceeds.
